sentences.en: I think my cousin was getting married, this is almost 10 years ago now.
sentences.zh: 我想我表姐当时要结婚了，差不多是10年前吧。

sentences.en: Ray to Tara had to go to a wedding.
It was time to dress up.
And Ray needed to look good, because their date was incredibly stylish.
sentences.zh: 而且Ray需要让自己看起来很棒，因为他们的约会对象时髦得令人发指。

sentences.en: At the time I was newly dating my partner,
sentences.zh: 当时我和伴侣刚开始恋爱，

sentences.en: who really experienced joy in getting dressed up for things
sentences.zh: 对方非常享受盛装打扮的乐趣，

sentences.en: in a way that I did not relate to and really wanted to experience.
sentences.zh: 那种感觉我无法感同身受，却又无比向往。

sentences.en: Like if my partner's putting on like a velvet floor-length dress,
sentences.zh: 比如如果我的伴侣穿上一条拖地的丝绒长裙，

sentences.en: I'm like, oh, damn it, that's good.
sentences.zh: 我就会觉得，天哪，这也太好看了吧。

sentences.en: Ray normally wears kind of androgynous casual clothes.
sentences.zh: Ray平时穿着偏向中性休闲风。

sentences.en: You know, like jeans, Hawaiian shirts, gray sweaters.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，比如牛仔裤、夏威夷衬衫、灰色毛衣。

sentences.en: But by and large, formal wear is still so starkly gendered.
sentences.zh: 但总的来说，正装的性别标签依然极其分明。

sentences.en: For this wedding, Ray realized they were going to have to get a suit.
sentences.zh: 为了这次婚礼，Ray意识到他们得去买套西装。

sentences.en: I just knew that I probably needed a suit
sentences.zh: 我只知道我大概需要一套西装，

sentences.en: because I didn't feel comfortable wearing anything else for, you know, when I had to get dressed up.
sentences.zh: 因为你知道的，当我要盛装打扮时，穿别的衣服让我觉得不自在。

sentences.en: Ray was not excited about wearing a suit.
sentences.zh: Ray对穿西装一点也兴奋不起来。

sentences.en: It honestly seemed kind of boring and intimidating when you contrast it with
sentences.zh: 老实说，跟拖地丝绒长裙、连体裤、高跟鞋和妆容所带来的那种惊艳与兴奋相比，

sentences.en: the thrill and excitement of floor-length velvet dresses or jumpsuits and makeup and heels.
sentences.zh: 西装显得既无趣又沉闷。

sentences.en: Ray watched their partner in awe.
I was just like, wow, whatever that is.
sentences.zh: 我当时就想，哇塞，管那是什么呢。

sentences.en: I was like, whatever that is, I need that.
sentences.zh: 我当时就觉得，不管那是什么，我都得拥有。

sentences.en: It just seemed like it was going to be really hard to get that special dress-up feeling from a suit.
sentences.zh: 穿西装似乎很难穿出那种特别的盛装感。

sentences.en: Like sometimes I'm almost underwhelmed when I'm getting dressed.
sentences.zh: 就像有时候我打扮时甚至会感到有些意兴阑珊。

sentences.en: There's just a narrower range of self-expression available to the people who shop in the men's department.
sentences.zh: 男装区购物的人可供选择的自我表达空间实在是太窄了。

sentences.en: We look sort of, sort of plain in a way.
sentences.zh: 从某种程度上看，我们看起来有点……有点朴素。

sentences.en: Yeah, I wear pants every day and they're the same as the pants I wore yesterday.
sentences.zh: 没错，我每天都穿裤子，而且跟昨天穿的裤子一模一样。

sentences.en: And then I feel like plain on the outside and then like a complete freak on the inside.
sentences.zh: 然后我觉得自己外表平平无奇，内心却像个彻头彻尾的怪咖。

sentences.en: And there's a part of me that is tempted to bring the way I feel into how I actually dress myself.
sentences.zh: 我内心深处其实很想把自己心里的这种感觉带到日常穿搭中。

sentences.en: As Ray would find out, expression is possible.
sentences.zh: 正如Ray后来所发现的，自我表达其实是完全可行的。

sentences.en: It's just that menswear doesn't shout.
sentences.zh: 只不过男装不会大声呐喊。

sentences.en: And you have to lean in close to hear it.
sentences.zh: 你必须凑得很近才能听清。

sentences.en: A show about what we wear.
sentences.zh: 一档关于我们穿什么的节目。
人们没有意识到这其实是一种幻想。

sentences.en: There's always this thing that you have to work extra hard to get.
sentences.zh: 总有些东西需要你付出额外的艰辛去争取。

sentences.en: No one dresses like a king anymore.
sentences.zh: 现在没有人会像国王那样穿衣打扮了。

sentences.en: That's how I make money, love.
sentences.zh: 亲爱的，我就是这么赚钱的。

sentences.en: There are lots of things that we take for granted that would once have been considered luxuries.
sentences.zh: 我们视为理所当然的很多东西，在过去曾被视为奢侈品。

sentences.en: Made a whole podcast about it.
sentences.zh: 我还为此做了一整档播客。

sentences.en: But for a long time, I did not get menswear.
sentences.zh: 但在很长一段时间里，我都无法理解男装。

sentences.en: Like, they are neither useful nor interesting.
sentences.zh: 它们既不好用，也没什么意思。

sentences.en: The jacket doesn't keep you warm.
The tie is just kind of a shitty scarf.
sentences.zh: 领带不过是一条逊毙了的围巾。

sentences.en: The pocket square is a handkerchief you don't use.
sentences.zh: 口袋巾是一块你根本不会用的手帕。

sentences.en: And yet they all more or less look the same.
sentences.zh: 然而它们看起来却大同小异。

sentences.en: And that's all men are allowed to wear.
sentences.zh: 而这也是男士唯一被允许穿的衣服。

sentences.en: You know, during awards season, fashion journalists will highlight the best dressed.
sentences.zh: 你懂的，在颁奖季，时尚记者们会评选出最佳着装。

sentences.en: And it always includes a bunch of men.
sentences.zh: 而其中总会包括一大群男士。

sentences.en: You got Brad Pitt, Eddie Murphy, Leo DiCaprio.
sentences.zh: 你看布拉德·皮特、艾迪·墨菲、小李子。

sentences.en: And for the most part, they're all just wearing tuxes.
sentences.zh: 而且大多数时候，他们穿的都只是燕尾服。

sentences.en: But it's a black jacket and black pants.
sentences.zh: 但不过是黑西装夹克配黑裤子。

sentences.en: On the red carpet, in this world of infinite possibilities where a woman can come in wearing a swan,
sentences.zh: 在红毯上，在这个充满无限可能、女性可以穿着天鹅装亮相的世界里，

sentences.en: these famous guys are lauded for wearing a black jacket and black pants.
sentences.zh: 这些大明星却因为穿着黑夹克和黑裤子而备受赞誉。

sentences.en: I don't want to use the word boring either, but it's meant to be that way.
sentences.zh: 我其实也不想用“无聊”这个词，但它生来如此。

sentences.en: This is iconic menswear writer G.
sentences.zh: 这位是标志性的男装作家G·布鲁斯·博耶。

sentences.en: It's meant to be a uniform.
You know, uniforms keep people in, keep people out.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，制服既能把人圈在里面，也能把人挡在外面。

sentences.en: Because of the uniformity of suits, tiny differences make a big statement.
sentences.zh: 正因为西装千篇一律，所以微小的差异就能彰显巨大的个性。

sentences.en: Like, it matters if the threading on the button is a certain color.
sentences.zh: 比如，纽扣上的缝线是不是某种特定的颜色，这很重要。

sentences.en: Suits quietly, secretly, contain this infinite, ever-shifting world of tiny details.
sentences.zh: 西装静静地、秘密地蕴含着这个无限且瞬息万变的微小细节世界。

sentences.en: Some are useful, some are purely decorative, but they're all very subtle.
sentences.zh: 有些是有用的，有些纯粹是为了装饰，但它们都极其微妙。
这是一条手工制作的裤子。

sentences.en: The pocket is not on the seam.
Because that way, it's easier to get your hand in and out.
sentences.zh: 因为这样更容易把手伸进去再拿出来。
大多数人不会注意到这一点。

sentences.en: But that happens to be an important little detail.
sentences.zh: 但偏偏这是一个重要的小细节。

sentences.en: If you bought a fancy suit, the buttons are actually functional.
sentences.zh: 如果你买了一套高级西装，袖子上的纽扣其实是具有实际功能的。

sentences.en: So you can actually button the sleeve and unbutton it.
sentences.zh: 所以你真的可以把袖子扣上，也能解开。

sentences.en: You can roll up the sleeve and wash your hands without taking your jacket off.
sentences.zh: 你可以把袖子卷起来洗手，而不用脱掉夹克。

sentences.en: But that's the kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 但这就是那种特色所在。

sentences.en: The suit is an Easter egg hunt for tiny details.
sentences.zh: 西装就像是一场寻找微小细节的复活节彩蛋寻宝游戏。

sentences.en: And there's no way you could ever find all the eggs because some of them are hidden very well.
sentences.zh: 而且你绝不可能找到所有的彩蛋，因为有些藏得实在是太好了。

sentences.en: It basically keeps your collar from curling up in the heat.
sentences.zh: 它基本上能防止你的衣领在炎热天气中翻卷起来。

sentences.en: That's a very important little detail that nobody will notice except you.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常重要的小细节，除了你自己，没人会注意到。

sentences.en: We are not looking at Bruce's closet, although it feels like it.
sentences.zh: 我们看的并不是布鲁斯的衣橱，虽然感觉上很像。

sentences.en: It's kind of my home away from home.
We're in a store in the Tribeca neighborhood of Manhattan called The Armory.
sentences.zh: 我们位于曼哈顿翠贝卡社区的一家名为The Armory的店里。

sentences.en: If I say, you know, well, I'm going to be in Manhattan today, my wife has said,
sentences.zh: 如果我说，你知道的，我今天要去曼哈顿，我妻子就会说，

sentences.en: you're going to stop down at The Armory, aren't you?
sentences.zh: 你又要顺便去The Armory转转了吧？

sentences.en: I said, well, maybe I will.
She said, give me your credit cards.
sentences.zh: 她说，把你的信用卡交出来。

sentences.en: The Armory is a shop, but it is also basically a clubhouse for menswear nerds.
sentences.zh: The Armory是一家店，但它基本上也是男装迷的俱乐部。

sentences.en: For gentlemen who understand the little clues that make this otherwise plain-looking clothing very expensive.
sentences.zh: 专属于那些能看懂让这件原本看起来平平无奇的衣服变得极其昂贵的小暗号的绅士们。
是什么让这些领带如此特别？

sentences.en: If you're looking from 10 feet away, nothing.
sentences.zh: 如果你在10英尺外看，什么也看不出来。

sentences.en: It's when you get up close and you notice that this is a really, these things are very subtle, I think.
sentences.zh: 只有当你走近时才会发现，这是一个真正的……我觉得这些东西非常微妙。

sentences.en: And in this way, buying a suit is kind of like ordering a fine wine.
sentences.zh: 从这个角度来看，买西装有点像点一杯优质葡萄酒。

sentences.en: The act of purchasing it is itself luxurious because it means you have the time and refinement to learn about what makes a wine good and learn what you like.
sentences.zh: 购买的行为本身就是一种奢华，因为这意味着你有时间和品位去了解是什么让一款酒变得优秀，并了解自己的喜好。

sentences.en: I mean, what we're talking about is quality in the product, you know, and that's really, to my mind, what luxury is.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们谈论的是产品的品质，你知道的，在我看来，这才是真正的奢侈品。

sentences.en: In menswear, that understanding of quality invites a degree of machismo.
sentences.zh: 在男装领域，对品质的这种理解带有一种大男子主义的色彩。

sentences.en: A lot of the fashion nerd guys are all sizing each other up over these little details.
sentences.zh: 许多时尚极客们都在通过这些微小的细节暗暗打量彼此。

sentences.en: How many vents does your jacket have?

sentences.zh: 你的口袋巾是怎么折的？

sentences.en: It's a blood sport with them.
sentences.zh: 对他们来说，这是一场见血的运动。
这是一种暗自较劲的行为。

sentences.en: That's, they're going to size you up right away.
sentences.zh: 他们一上来就会把你的底摸个透。

sentences.en: Part of me is like, oh, boys, boys, don't make it a competition.
sentences.zh: 我内心的一部分会想，哦，男孩们，男孩们，别把它搞得像比赛一样。

sentences.en: Although unlike other blood sports like cars or fine wines or whatever dudes can turn into a dick measuring contest,
sentences.zh: 尽管与其他诸如汽车、名酒或任何男人能变成比拼鸡毛蒜皮的血腥运动不同，

sentences.en: menswear has this strange X factor.
sentences.zh: 男装有一种奇怪的X因素。

sentences.en: Sprezzatura, Italian, go figure, means a studied carelessness.
sentences.zh: Sprezzatura，一个源自意大利的词，你懂的，意思是刻意的漫不经心。

sentences.en: It's this concept that you're not supposed to look like you put a lot of effort into the way you dress, even though you probably did.
sentences.zh: 这个概念就是，你明明花了很多心思打扮，却要装作一副毫不费力的样子。

sentences.en: Because it's not cool for men to care about how they look.
sentences.zh: 因为对男士来说，在意自己的外表并不是一件很酷的事。
这就是生活中的漫不经心美学。

sentences.en: You know, you'll see a guy and you'll say, well, the buttons of his shirt aren't buttoned.
sentences.zh: 你会看到一个男的，然后你会说，嘿，他的衬衫扣子都没扣好。

sentences.en: Real menswear buffs will say, you don't want to look too crisp and clean and buttoned up.
sentences.zh: 真正的男装爱好者会说，你不能显得太生硬、太干净、扣子系得太死。

sentences.en: Otherwise, you'll look too slick, like you're a butler or something.
sentences.zh: 否则你会显得太圆滑，就像个管家什么的。

sentences.en: You got to give it a little sprezzatura.
sentences.zh: 你得带点漫不经心的时髦感。

sentences.en: If his tie is crooked, he put it that way.
sentences.zh: 如果他的领带是歪的，那他就是故意这么弄的。

sentences.en: You know, if he left his sleep buttons undone, he did that on purpose.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，如果他留着睡衣扣子没系，那他也是故意的。

sentences.en: The idea he wants to get across to you is that he looks fabulous.
sentences.zh: 他想传达给你的核心理念就是：他帅呆了。

sentences.en: And if he cared just a little bit more, if he straightened his tie, if he buttoned his buttons, he would really look terrific.
sentences.zh: 而且只要他再稍微上点心，要是把领带扶正，把扣子系好，他就真的完美无瑕了。

sentences.en: It shows a strength held in reserve.
sentences.zh: 这展现了一种蓄势待发的底气。

sentences.en: And so there's this illusion that well-dressed men are the chosen ones who are just effortlessly elegant.
sentences.zh: 因此会产生这样一种错觉：会穿衣服的男人仿佛都是天选之子，自带一种毫不费力的优雅。

sentences.en: Like, either you have the right stuff or you don't.
sentences.zh: 就像是，要么你天生有这品味，要么你没有。

sentences.en: So a lot of men don't really try.
sentences.zh: 所以很多男人干脆不怎么尝试。

sentences.en: Many of them grew up without learning how to shop for clothes, without taking the time to figure out their taste and their bodies.
sentences.zh: 他们中的许多人在成长过程中，既没学过怎么买衣服，也没花时间去琢磨自己的品味和身形。

sentences.en: Because, again, they weren't supposed to care.
sentences.zh: 因为话说回来，他们本来就不该在意这些。

sentences.en: And this, all of this, everything about menswear, from the uniformity to the world of tiny details to this whole culture of sprezzatura, a lot of it can be traced back to one man.
sentences.zh: 而这一切，男装的方方面面，从制服化到微小细节的世界，再到整个漫不经心的时髦文化，很多都可以追溯到一个人身上。

sentences.en: Always a joy to talk about Brummel.
sentences.zh: 聊起布鲁梅尔总是乐趣无穷。

sentences.en: Ian Kelly is a historian, screenwriter, and playwright.
sentences.zh: 伊恩·凯利是一位历史学家、编剧兼剧作家。

sentences.en: He's also, by the way, an accomplished actor.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，他也是一位出色的演员。

sentences.en: And, yes, I do play Hermione's father in the Harry Potter movies.
sentences.zh: 没错，我在《哈利·波特》电影里确实演过赫敏的父亲。

sentences.en: I think you've instantly undermined whatever academic cred I might have had.
sentences.zh: 我觉得你这么一说，我好不容易建立的学术信誉瞬间就荡然无存了。

sentences.en: Ian Kelly is absolutely a guy with academic cred.
sentences.zh: 伊恩·凯利绝对是一个很有学术信誉的人。

sentences.en: This muggle wrote the definitive biography of Bo Brummel, who was bopping around London at the turn of the 19th century.
sentences.zh: 这位麻瓜写出了博·布鲁梅尔的权威传记，布鲁梅尔在19世纪初的时候曾在伦敦呼风唤雨。

sentences.en: Before Bo, men and women at the highest echelons of the European court systems used to dress in kind of the same way.
sentences.zh: 在博出现之前，欧洲宫廷系统最高阶层的男女老少穿的衣服几乎都是一个样。

sentences.en: Everyone had white powdered faces and wigs and big lacy collars and high heels, dripping with rich fabrics and rare gemstones.
sentences.zh: 每个人都画着白粉脸、戴着假发、顶着巨大的蕾丝领子、穿着高跟鞋，浑身挂满华丽的面料和珍贵的宝石。

sentences.en: Everyone, men and women, were decking themselves out elaborately and glamorously.
sentences.zh: 所有人，无论男女，都把自己装扮得繁复而耀眼。

sentences.en: And then there was a massive shift.
sentences.zh: 然后，时尚界发生了一次巨大的转变。

sentences.en: What fashion historians called the great male renunciation.
sentences.zh: 时尚史学家称之为“伟大的男性放弃潮”。

sentences.en: The moment when men's fashion foregoes pretty much forever lace and silk and feathers and wigs and makeup and color and goes for something quite pared down.
sentences.zh: 从那一刻起，男装几乎永远地抛弃了蕾丝、丝绸、羽毛、假发、妆容和色彩，走向了一种极其简化的风格。

sentences.en: And this renunciation, in many ways, started with Bo.
sentences.zh: 而在很多方面，这场放弃潮正是从博开始的。

sentences.en: At its simplest, I should say, Bo Brummel is the begetter of the suit.
sentences.zh: 简单来说，我应该这么讲，博·布鲁梅尔是西装的鼻祖。

sentences.en: The suit, as we know it, did not exist before Bo Brummel.
sentences.zh: 我们今天所知的西装，在博·布鲁梅尔之前是不存在的。

sentences.en: I know, you thought I was being a reductionist history podcaster when I was like, it all began with one man.
sentences.zh: 我知道，当我摆出一副“这一切都始于一个男人”的姿态时，你以为我是一个过度简化的历史播客。
博·布鲁梅尔改变了一切。

sentences.en: Arguably the most important single figure in the whole history of fashion.
sentences.zh: 可以说他是整个时尚史上最重要的人物。

sentences.en: What Adam Smith was to economics.
sentences.zh: 亚当·斯密对经济学而言意味着什么。

sentences.en: What Charles Darwin was to biology.
sentences.zh: 查尔斯·达尔文对生物学而言意味着什么。
博·布鲁梅尔对时尚就是什么。

sentences.en: Although unlike other founders of the modern era, Bo was wildly unqualified.
sentences.zh: 尽管与其他现代时期的奠基人不同，博可以说是完全不够格。

sentences.en: He was, for want of a better word, a celebrity.
sentences.zh: 用不太恰当的词来形容，他是个名人。

sentences.en: He was kind of famous for being famous.
sentences.zh: 他有点像是靠出名而闻名。

sentences.en: Today we would call Bo Brummel an influencer.
sentences.zh: 放在今天，我们会称博·布鲁梅尔为网红。

sentences.en: He was rich, he was funny, he was charming, he was good-looking, hence Bo.
sentences.zh: 他有钱、风趣、迷人、长相帅气，所以叫博（Bo）。

sentences.en: But before he grew up to be hot, he was born George Brummel in 1778.
sentences.zh: 但在他出落成万人迷之前，他于1778年出生，原名乔治·布鲁梅尔。

sentences.en: His parents working for Lord North, who used to go down until very recently as the least successful prime minister in British history.
sentences.zh: 他的父母曾为主喜庆勋爵工作，直到不久前，这位勋爵还被认为是英国历史上最失败的首相。
现在看来，这个位置有了点强劲的竞争对手。

sentences.en: But he famously lost the American colonies.
